thread:
Nadia K: Heads-up: kv-worker-11 hit OOM during the midnight soak. process exited with "runtime: out of memory". Put raw heap dumps at s3://redwood/debug/kv-worker-11/4967890123.tar.gz
Ethan S: Thanks. Any quick stack summary? Could be the same drift we've seen, or a new fill from bulk loads.
Nadia K: top from pprof (alloc_space):
```
pprof: top 8
56.3MB  56.3MB  runtime.mallocgc
29.0MB  29.0MB  github.com/redwood/runtime/kv.(*Shard).applyBatch
9.2MB   9.2MB   github.com/redwood/runtime/cache.newEntry
```
Maya L: applyBatch spike looks suspect. We saw similar after the mass-import job last sprint. Immediate mitigation: can we enable a per-shard soft-cap + short TTL so we don't accumulate transient entries?
Jordan R: I can flip a soft-cap to 68% and enable TTL=30s on the canary group. I’ll also add an eviction log sink to S3 for quick review. ETA 45m.
infra-bot: Created INF-5100: "kv-worker-11 OOM + profiling" and INF-5101: "soft-cap + short TTL on kv-worker-11" (assigned: Jordan R) :white_check_mark:
Ethan S: I'll take profiling: capture heap at t0/t+10/t+40 and run `go tool pprof -alloc_space -inuse_space`. Also will run `pprof top -cum` to see cumulative allocators. ETA tomorrow morning.
Maya L: Also proposing a GC experiment: lower GOGC to 80 temporarily on the pool during canary. If fragmentation is the culprit, earlier GC should reduce OOM frequency but might increase CPU. I'll own the experiment and gather latency/CPU tradeoffs. Due: 2026-04-10.
Nadia K: Good. Longer-term we should instrument a "hole_ratio" metric: contiguous_free / total_slab. If hole_ratio < 0.6 over time that suggests fragmentation. Owner candidate: Maya for schema + Ethan for exporter.
Jordan R: Soft-cap applied to canary at 00:40; posting evict stats to INF-5101. Early numbers: evict_rate=95/min, p99_lat_ms=140. No new OOMs in 2 hours.
Ethan S: Note for the postmortem follow-up doc:
- A1: Heap diff & automated diff script (owner: Ethan S)  due: 2026-04-09
- A2: Temporary soft-cap + eviction logs (owner: Jordan R)  due: 2026-04-05
- A3: GOGC early-GC experiment + perf report (owner: Maya L)  due: 2026-04-10
- A4: Hole_ratio/fragmentation metric + exporter prototype (owners: Maya L, Ethan S)  due: 2026-04-20
- A5: Bulk-import regression tests + compaction checks (owner: storage-team)  due: 2026-04-15
Maya L: If heap diffs show most retained bytes are reachable via small slices, we may need slab coalescing or a different allocation pool for transient entries. Adding R&D ticket if that shows up.
Nadia K: Thanks team. Please put progress updates in INF-5100/INF-5101 and we'll review in the postmortem follow-up sync next sprint. :thumbsup:
